Belgrave's day did not get off to a very good start, for with four to score in the team event we were only able to field three runners - Eric Penny, Mike Smithers and Roy Bagley.
Eric Penny was fourth in the mile, whilst new members Mike Smithers and Roy Bagley both finished fifth in the first and second string 440 event with times of 58.5 and 59.5 respectively.
In the junior events Eric Penny recorded his fastest mile to date with 4m.43s. for fourth place. Although running well, Mike Smithers and Derek Wade failed to reach the final of the 100 yds.

Our junior Captain, Brian Kolbe performed creditably in both the 220 and 440 and is improving each time out. Eric Penny ran a very well judged race to win the mile in 4m.45·7s., an encouraging early season time.

In the junior match Brian Kolbe (2m.4·5s.) was our only winner although Eric Penny was narrowly beaten in the mile. The junior section must be hungrily awaiting the arrival of some of our promising youths.

Eric Penny ran well on Friday evening to qualify for the Junior mile final but found the opposition too strong next day. The first four broke the Best Championship Performance and the first seven were inside 4m.23s.!
Brian Kolbe was third in the 880 with 2:7.0 and Eric Penny 4th in the mile with 4:46.4. The Juniors followed the example of the seniors by winning the relay.

Eric Penny gained a valuable 10 points with a win in the junior ¾ mile, and a walk-over in the 660 yards. Alan Jackson had a fine win from Buchanan (HHH) in the 300 yards after having finished third, with 10.6 secs., in the short sprint.

Our four runners were Roy Bagley, Mike Smithers, Eddie Gaze and Eric Penny in that order. In the Surrey County Junior Championships at Warlingham on January 13th, Chris Steer (8th) Tony Fairclough (10th), Eric Penny (28th) and Philip King (42nd) were placed 6th in the team race.

Chris Steer led our men home in 57th place, closely followed by Tony Fairclough. Eric Penny 127th and an under-trained Cyril Forey 178th completed our team. We shall do much better in this Championship in future years.

Tony Fairclough proved too strong for the other two youths and finished third, a minute behind the winner. Eric Penny and Philip King were two of several runners that went off course, but fortunately this did not affect the Championship result.

Chris Steer finished first for us but after his recent good form was rather disappointing, Eric Penny and Tony Fairclough battled gamely on, whilst Cyril Forey gave us ample proof of his lack of training.

Positions remained fairly static on the fourth stage with Eric Penny and Howerd Satchell recording the same times. Next off for the 'A' team was John Thresher who passed a struggling Clive Shippen (running for the 'B' team) to bring us up to 8th.

It was good to see Eric Penny back in action again and we hope to see more of him on the road. 'Glimpy' Jones is also enjoying a new lease of life at present and "out to get" the elusive Charlie Smart.
Eric Penny and Chris Keavey again continued to show an improvement, whilst Don Maclean found the course, the heat and achilles trouble a little too much for one afternoon.

Of our other runners, and we had 25 out all together, the bouquets went to Bob Glover and Eric Penny. Bob was showing some of his old fire again and moved very well to finish 96th, and Eric continued his steady improvement to record a best ever placing of 118th.
These three were followed home in quick succession by Eric Penny, Bernard Merry and John Hall who thus disproved the suggestion that Belgravians do not know how to 'pack' these days.

Up and coming Pat O'Connor put in another very strong run whilst Eric Penny took nearly two minutes off his last year's time.
